prompts.title: Slow Approach on the Duel
prompts.prompt: Using the input image as reference, perform a slow cinematic push-in with the camera over 6 seconds in vertical 9:16. Ease gently toward the central action so the primary player and ball grow slightly larger in frame while the background falls away with natural depth. Include subtle breathing in the camera path—tiny vertical drift and micro-stabilization—so the move feels handheld and alive. Where the input image supports it, animate plausible ball roll or player weight shift, keeping anatomy, limbs and kit details stable. Preserve original colours, crests and illustrative character. Keep faces legible and leave the lower frame clear for subtitles. No text, no new stadium elements, no invented people.

prompts.title: Lateral Glide Across the Pitch
prompts.prompt: From the input image, animate a smooth lateral camera tracking shot lasting 6 seconds, rendered in vertical 9:16. The camera slides sideways at a restrained speed with mild parallax: foreground figures move slightly faster than the background plane, giving coherent depth. Sports movement stays physically plausible—only motion the reference image already supports, such as a running stride, planted foot or the ball travelling along the turf. Maintain stable anatomy, consistent kit colours, crests and flags exactly as supplied. Faces remain sharp and readable; keep the bottom of the frame free for subtitles. Hyperrealistic texture, gentle motion blur only on fast elements. No generated text, narration or music, and no invented players or events.

prompts.title: Subtle Arc Around the Action
prompts.prompt: Apply a subtle camera arc to the input image: a gentle orbit of only a few degrees around the main subject over 6 seconds, output in vertical 9:16. The slight change in viewpoint should reveal believable depth layering between players, ball and background while preserving the original composition and perspective logic. Include small natural movements—breathing sway, minor parallax, hair or jersey reacting lightly to motion—so the frame feels alive without exaggeration. Never rotate to expose faces the reference image does not show; keep all visible faces legible and anatomically stable. Retain exact kit colours, crests and flags. Reserve the lower frame for subtitles. No text overlays, no invented stadium details, people or events; audio is added downstream.

prompts.title: Controlled Dolly Back to Composition
prompts.prompt: Starting tight on the key subject of the input image, execute a controlled pull-out with the camera backing away over 6 seconds in vertical 9:16. The dolly should resolve smoothly back into the original reference composition, revealing only what the input image already contains—no extra stands, crowds, signage or pitch details invented beyond frame. Motion stays restrained: slight camera breathing, gentle parallax between existing depth layers, and only plausible player or ball movement supported by the source. Preserve stable anatomy, original faces (kept legible), kit colours, crests and flags. Keep the lower third open for subtitles and avoid any generated text. Hyperrealistic rendering throughout; narration, music and sound are added downstream.

prompts.title: Rack Focus Between Existing Subjects
prompts.prompt: Using the input image, perform a smooth rack focus between existing subjects—shifting attention from the foreground player or ball to another element already present in the scene, or vice versa—across 6 seconds in vertical 9:16. Pair the focus pull with a gentle camera reposition: a small drift or tilt that stays within the original framing and introduces no new background content. The transition should be restrained and soft, with realistic bokeh and smooth focus falloff, never a hard cut. Keep anatomy stable, faces legible whenever they are in focus, and kit colours, crests and flags exactly as in the reference. Leave the lower frame clear for subtitles. No generated text, no invented people or events, no audio.
